prior.title: Several clear errors got no coaching
prior.expected: 'I have problem', 'because is too hot', 'water is not hot in shower' noted in the recap
prior.got: Only 'not work' became a moment; the recap lists one fix
evidence: #2 'I have problem'; #4 'because is too hot'; #6 'the water is not hot in shower'; #9 '1 moment to keep'

prior.title: Clear errors got no stop and no held fix; recap shows none
prior.expected: 'the heating is not work' and 'because is very cold' noted as a moment or a held fix on the recap
prior.got: rawMoments kind none for all three turns; moments and heldFixes empty; recap shows only a hidden line
evidence: #2 'the heating is not work'; #3 'I cannot sleep because is very cold... two blanket'; #6 recap lists no fix

prior.title: Conversation ended after three replies
prior.got: Mission done after the third reply, partner offered room twelve at once
evidence: #5 'Mission done. See what you did tonight.' after three learner replies

criteria.evidence: Level set by fixture; no placement in J3.
#2 'Name the problem and how it affects your sleep'; #3 'Ask for a new room or an extra blanket' are plain A2.
Petra never asked for a repeat or said she did not understand.
#1 plan topics: cold room, booking, station, restaurant, travel agency are work situations (5 of 6).
#5 'I want a different room' is correct but is a guest's phrase; Petra is the receptionist and gets nothing for the desk. #3 'I want other room' got no stop.
Nothing in #1–#9 is unsuitable for children.

done.evidence: #8 'Mission done' after three learner replies, with Mira's 'Is seven o'clock good for you?' unanswered; the journey asked for about eight.
All four Mira turns are short A2 lines, e.g. #4 'Yes, I can help you with that. Is the heat OK in your room?'
One stop (#5–#7), correct: 'I only want other room' → 'I want a different room'. Precision 1/1; no overload.
#9 recap shows '3 spoken · 0 written replies · 1 moment to keep' and the fix.

findings.title: Conversation ended after three replies
findings.expected: About eight learner turns of practice
findings.got: Mission done after the third reply; Mira's last question was never answered
findings.evidence: #8 'Mission done. See what you did tonight.' after three learner replies; Mira: 'Is seven o'clock good for you?' left open.
findings.suggested_acceptance: The mission closes only after enough turns, or after the learner answers the last question.

findings.title: Petra plays the guest, not the receptionist
findings.expected: Phrases for Petra's own job, such as handling a complaint at the desk
findings.got: She says 'I want a different room' as the complaining guest
findings.evidence: #2 Mira is 'hotel receptionist'; #5 the fix is a guest phrase.
findings.suggested_acceptance: A hotel-worker learner takes the staff role, or the recap offers the staff-side phrase.

findings.title: Same error missed on its first appearance
findings.expected: 'I want other room' in #3 noted when it first appeared
findings.got: No moment at #3; it was caught only when repeated at #4
findings.evidence: rawMoments turn 3 kind none; turn 5 kind fix.
findings.suggested_acceptance: A repeated clear error is flagged, or held for the recap, on first sight.

findings.title: Patient, short A2 partner and a gentle moment
findings.got: Mira's lines are simple; the moment lets Petra retry without being tested
findings.evidence: #4 partner lines; #5–#7 'Say it again, your way', 'You fixed “i want”'.

findings.title: Partner asked about heat in a noise complaint
findings.expected: Follow-up that fits the stated noise problem
findings.got: Mira asks 'Is the heat OK in your room?' because the plan topic is a cold room
findings.suggested_acceptance: The partner follows the learner's problem, not the preset topic.

judge.voice: Sorry, it was gentle with me and I liked that. Mira spoke slowly and simply, and when I made a mistake it did not make me feel stupid. I said it again and carried on, and that was fine. But it finished after only three answers. I wanted to say yes to seven o'clock and it said "mission done". That is too short to really practise. Also I was the guest, asking for a room. At work I am the one who gives the room! I need phrases for the desk tomorrow, like what to say to an angry guest. It only fixed one thing, though I made the same mistake twice. Nothing worried me as a mother. I would try it again for fifteen minutes, but it has to be longer and work-shaped. Maybe I tell Klára.

prior.evidence: #5–#9 the main error was stopped and kept; only the first 'I want other room' at #3 got nothing.
A stop shown at #5 and the recap at #9 lists it: '1 moment to keep'.

verdictWhy.text: D1 failed: #8 'Mission done' after three learner replies, with Mira's 'Is seven o'clock good for you?' unanswered; the journey asked for about eight.
verdictWhy.check: The Character starts a conversation from their plan and keeps it going for several turns.

verdictWhy.text: C5 failed: #5 'I want a different room' is correct but is a guest's phrase; Petra is the receptionist and gets nothing for the desk. #3 'I want other room' got no stop.

findings.expected: A coaching note on the reply she struggled with, helping her say or read the number.
findings.got: Coach quotes her first reply, which was fine, and advises 'Here is my booking number' without saying how to read a number.
findings.evidence: #9 'You said Sorry, I have a booking for two nights.' while she was stuck at #8 on 'Your booking number, please?'.
findings.suggested_acceptance: The note quotes the latest stuck reply and gives a usable phrase for the gap, such as reading digits aloud.

findings.title: Clear learner errors got no moment
findings.expected: Fixes for 'under other name', 'I have it in email' and the 'I look' pattern, at least held for the recap.
findings.got: Only one moment shown and no held fixes.
findings.evidence: rawMoments for turns 4, 8, 10, 14 are kind none. Her errors include 'under other name', 'I have it in email' and 'check out'.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Recall rises, or held fixes appear on the recap.

findings.title: Recap keeps the progress picture honest
findings.expected: Supported replies are not counted as independent.
findings.got: '6 on your own · 1 with help', with the helped turn marked supported.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Keep the supported flag tied to cue and coach use.

findings.title: Clerk is patient and at A2
findings.got: 'Please read me the number. Take your time.' All nine partner turns are at A2.

judge.voice: Sorry, my English is not good, but I try. The clerk Tom was patient, "Take your time", and that I liked. A booking problem is exactly my work, so I would use it again after the kids sleep. But the help button gave me the same sentence again and again, "I have a booking for two nights", even when he asked my name and my number. That did not help me. The coach talked about my first answer, not about where I was stuck. When I tried again, the question was almost the same, and I still said "I don't know". "I'm looking" is a good phrase and I can use it at the desk. But many of my mistakes, like "other name", nobody corrected. I trust the recap, it says honestly one answer with help. Nothing worried me as a mother. Useful, but the help must fit the question. I would tell a colleague maybe.

prior.evidence: #10 'Try it again' label appears once and clears by #11. The replay question is on the booking number she was coached on, though it is not truly fresh.
#12 moment offers only '[button: Back to the conversation]', then #13 'Please read me the number.' and the fix is never retried.
#3, #6, #7, #8 all show 'Try: I have a booking for two nights. Can you check again, please?' for different questions.
#9 coach quotes the earlier 'Sorry, I have a booking for two nights.' while she was stuck on the booking number. The advice 'Here is my booking number' gives no way to say it.
#12 moment screen has only 'Back to the conversation', no fresh-question replay.
#9 Replay was pressed and #10 gave a replayed question 'What is your booking number?' before finishing at #17.

verdictWhy.text: D3 failed: #10 replay question 'What is your booking number?' is the same ask as #5 'Your booking number, please?', not a fresh question. Her answer 'I don't know. I have it in email' does not use the coached 'Here is my booking number.'
verdictWhy.check: Replaying the moment gives them a fresh question, and they answer it better than before.
